meta.title: Everything Beebo Entertainment is and offers
meta.how: Each feature has an availability label and evidence limits. Testing percentages refer to the dated checks in testing-status.json; published download versions and times come from the release feeds.

statusRules.Available: In a current download and usable today, and a person has run the main use on a real device or PC (the evidence line says what).
statusRules.Beta: In a current download or switchable today, but new, tested by automatic tests only, or with real problems found.
statusRules.In development: Being built, switched off, not in a current download, or never tried on the real equipment it needs.

areas.name: Windows server
areas.blurb: The Windows app that holds your library and serves it to your other screens.

areas.name: Android phone
areas.blurb: The Android phone and tablet app (test download, not on Google Play).

areas.name: Android TV and Beebo Auto

areas.name: Other TV and Apple platforms

areas.name: Computers, browsers and NAS

areas.name: Campsite Mode

areas.name: Trip Journal

areas.name: Online services
areas.blurb: Sign-in, browser games and the optional extras.

features.name: Installer and updates
features.evidence: A PC updated itself from 0.1.78 to 0.1.79 while idle on Oct 5; on Oct 13 the update check on a newer test build said up to date. Not tried: updating over an older version on a second PC. Windows may show a SmartScreen warning the first time. Oct 22: a Windows test PC updated itself from 0.1.98 to 0.1.99 and the app started normally.

features.name: Library folders, scanning and matching
features.evidence: Oct 22 test-build update: The browser repair has split delivery: the server portion is reported deployed at 6:49 AM Eastern on October 22, with a further TV-browser server repair at 7:24 AM; the desktop-player portion is in unpublished Windows 0.1.100. The affected PC and combined away-route repair still need retesting. Owner-reported on October 22: on a friend’s Samsung TV built-in browser, playback away from home and Skip intro worked after repeated Reconnect clicks; ordinary poster/sidebar navigation failed without that extra step, and Up next/Next were absent at the credits. The fixed-build retry, exact TV model, browser version and served build are unconfirmed. Earlier Chromecast viewing is a separate observation with sender details unconfirmed. No new tick or broad real-world pass. The reviewed web-player Next/Full screen work is not in public downloads. Pages that suppress referrer information and a modeled cross-tab edge case remain qualified. Android version-picker results do not verify the separate desktop version-heading issue.

features.name: Posters, details and cast (you add your own TMDB key)
features.evidence: Oct 5: titles, ratings and descriptions were shown with a trailer button (one check). A new PC with no key shows placeholder posters (seen Oct 13). Beebo does not include a shared key. Oct 21 on Windows 0.1.98 (a PC with no TMDB key): a folder's own poster, fanart and NFO files were not used, so test films showed "No poster"; the cause is not found yet.

features.name: Direct play and on-demand conversion to 1080p, 720p and 480p
features.evidence: Oct 5 and Oct 13: the original file played; in the browser player 720p, 480p and Auto switched and kept playing from the same second. The desktop app opens films in the PC's own player; in-app playback is the phone app and the browser.

features.name: Hardware-assisted conversion (graphics chip)
features.evidence: Intel Quick Sync was found and used on one PC (Oct 5). NVIDIA, AMD, Linux and Mac encoders are not tested. Optional HEVC and AV1 output are hardware-only or opt-in, off by default, and not tested on real hardware.

features.name: HDR to SDR conversion
features.evidence: Automatic tests only; no HDR film or HDR TV test is recorded.

features.name: HDR10+, Dolby Vision, Atmos and DTS:X passthrough
features.evidence: Not claimed. Being built.

features.name: Audio tracks and sound modes (stereo mix-down, dialogue focus, night mode)
features.evidence: Oct 13: two audio tracks and the sound modes were listed in the browser player. Nobody has listened to them. Oct 21 (Windows 0.1.98) and Oct 22 (Galaxy S25) lists of three audio tracks (two stereo, one 5.1) could be chosen; both runs were muted.

features.name: Subtitles: embedded, image subtitles and online search with your own key
features.evidence: Oct 21 on Windows 0.1.98: embedded English and Spanish tracks switched, and a sidecar English file showed its text, in the Beebo player on a test film. Oct 22 on the Galaxy S25 phone app: the player offered no way to choose embedded subtitles and did not show sidecar files. A fix is merged in the code; it is not released or retested. Online search was not tried.

features.name: Chapters, seek previews, skip intro and credits
features.evidence: Oct 21 on Windows 0.1.98: the chapter list showed four chapters and a jump to chapter 3 landed at 17 seconds. Oct 22 on the Galaxy S25 phone app: chapter buttons, a chapter list and tick marks worked. Seek previews and skip intro and credits were not tried.

features.name: Watchlist, favourites, Continue watching, playlists and smart playlists
features.evidence: Oct 5 and Oct 13: a title was added to and removed from the watchlist, a playlist was made and deleted, smart playlists listed their titles.

features.name: Collections, missing films and missing episodes
features.evidence: Oct 5 and Oct 13: collections showed which films are not in the library; on Oct 13 there were 101 collections with counts, search narrowed them, and missing aired episodes were listed (data from TVmaze).

features.name: Home layouts, 11 layout packs and 8 colour themes
features.evidence: Oct 13: all five Home layouts opened with real content; Customize layout save, cancel and reset worked. Oct 5: 11 layouts and 8 themes were offered.

features.name: Languages: English plus Spanish, French, German, Portuguese (Brazil) and Italian
features.evidence: The five translations were made with a machine's help; three more are previews. Oct 13: switching English to Spanish and back changed the whole app at once. No native speaker has read the wording. Oct 22: genre names switched to French, German and Spanish on two phones; parts of the phone player bar stay English in those languages.

features.name: Owner dashboard: sessions, bandwidth, health and user permissions
features.evidence: Oct 5 and Oct 13: the dashboard showed a playing stream, bandwidth, conversions, library counts and each person's controls.

features.name: Back up and restore settings
features.evidence: Automatic tests only.

features.name: Photos and phone backups: timeline, albums, map
features.evidence: Oct 22 test-build update: One desktop access-check repair covers both child-profile thumbnails and full pictures; separate Android changes cover wording, month-language updates and chip layout. RETEST-1: the S9+ child saw real thumbnails and full pictures, swiped between pictures, saw empty Videos wording, immediate Spanish month headings and fitting chips at 1.3 text size. These narrow passes on tester35 with Windows 0.1.100 supersede the earlier blank-picture failure for that setup. Map, removal, real pinch, full folder, backup/privacy and other devices remain unverified; Real device stays false.

features.name: Picture frame (a photo wall for a tablet or TV)
features.evidence: In Windows 0.1.98 and later, off until you turn it on. Oct 21 on Windows 0.1.98, with the wall page opened in the PC's own browser: 10 checks passed and 1 (link expiry) was not run. Not tried on a tablet, phone or TV, and not repeated on 0.1.99.

features.name: Kitchen announcements (messages to phones)
features.evidence: In Windows 0.1.97 and later, off by default. The Announce panel was opened read-only in English, French and German on Windows 0.1.98; no message was sent.

features.name: Space Saver: folder clean-up and encrypted private storage
features.evidence: Automatic tests only. It changes files, so it has not been tried on a real library.

features.name: Upload page and Beebo Inbox (watched drop folder)
features.evidence: The Upload screen opened on Oct 13. The Inbox is covered by automatic tests only; it never deletes your files.

features.name: Jellyfin-compatible mode (use Jellyfin apps with Beebo)
features.evidence: Off by default. Automatic tests only; not every compatible app has been tried.

features.name: Personal API keys, notifications, webhooks and metrics
features.evidence: Automatic tests only.

features.name: Switch to Beebo importers (Plex, Jellyfin, Emby, Kodi, Letterboxd)
features.evidence: The screen opened on Oct 13. No real import from another app is recorded.

features.name: Sharing watch and listen history to Trakt, Last.fm or ListenBrainz (opt-in)
features.evidence: Automatic tests only.

features.name: Start with Windows and read-only library folders
features.evidence: Opt-in. Automatic tests only; start with Windows has never been run through a real restart.

features.name: Personalized storybooks and story writing
features.evidence: The screens opened on Oct 13. Not tested beyond opening.

features.name: Remote Desktop (see and control the PC from a phone)
features.evidence: Off by default and never run on a real PC. The keyboard helper change is in Windows 0.1.97. What is left: real keyboard, mouse, viewing, approval, disconnect and revoke checks.

features.name: Story Studio (turn a story into a short cartoon on your own PC)
features.evidence: Owner only. Tried in the real packaged app on Oct 1 (a 64-second export with real computer voices). Only we have tried it.

features.name: Home Game Server panel
features.evidence: The panel opens (Oct 13) and shows Stopped. No game server has been run with players.

features.name: Read It To Me
features.evidence: In the Windows download; since Windows 0.1.88 (Oct 14, 2026) it can use a voice from the computer. Not tried by a person on a real PC.

features.name: Guest upload requests (a guest asks, you approve)
features.evidence: In Windows 0.1.88 and later (Oct 14, 2026): phones can send videos to the computer, and a guest can ask to add a video that the owner approves. Not tried by a person on real phones.

features.name: Keyboard and screen-reader support
features.evidence: Automatic tests only; no screen-reader pass is recorded.

features.name: Strong volume leveler
features.evidence: Being built.

features.name: Opening the app and the five tabs (Home, Browse, Library, Play, More)
features.evidence: Oct 22 test-build update: RETEST-1 reports no crash-log entries and retained sign-in on the three named phones using tester35 with Windows 0.1.100. This is not a new full five-tab or TalkBack pass. Historical ticks stay unchanged.

features.name: Playing films: resume, seek, pause and the quality menu
features.evidence: Oct 22 test-build update: RETEST-1 on tester35 with Windows 0.1.100: the S9+ Subtitle Test started promptly and played the 30-second clip twice; the landscape subtitle sheet and English/Spanish selection worked. On the S25, version selection between 1080p and 720p worked and 720p stayed selected. FAIL: listed/selected English and Spanish sidecar files drew no subtitle text. PARTIAL: online Next jumped to the next season once, then the expected same-season episode on three later tries; offline Next passed with existing downloads. Earlier unexplained Pixel Next behavior remains open; a stale queue is a hypothesis. The screen-off switch kept Android’s PLAYING state, not sound heard by a person. French player labels appeared on the Pixel.

features.name: Picture-in-picture
features.evidence: Oct 3: the owner's own hand test passed picture-in-picture on both phones. Oct 13 on the Galaxy S9+: the film floated over Home, kept playing, and tapping it returned to the full player. Oct 22 on tester34: picture-in-picture opened on the Galaxy S24 Ultra and the Pixel 3.

features.name: Keeping sound going with the screen off
features.evidence: Oct 13 on the S9+: with the default setting the sound stopped when the screen turned off; with the Screen off option on, it kept playing. Oct 22 on tester34: the switch moved into the Quality & audio sheet (off by default) and flipped on and off on the S25 and the Pixel 3 and was seen on the S24 Ultra (already on there); one later Pixel 3 run did not find it. Real screen-off sound with the switch on has not been tested on tester34. Making it the default is undecided.

features.name: Downloads for offline viewing, with delete
features.evidence: Oct 13 on the S9+: a 1.6 GB episode downloaded on Wi-Fi and was deleted, freeing the space. Oct 5: a downloaded episode played with Wi-Fi off. Smaller sizes were not offered for that file. Oct 22 on tester34: small test episodes downloaded in seconds and played with the phone offline. Next on a saved episode worked offline.

features.name: Pack for a trip (download planner)
features.evidence: Tried on a real phone on Oct 2; a full start-to-finish trip download still needs a real test.

features.name: Casting to a Chromecast TV
features.evidence: Oct 13 to a real Chromecast TV from two phones: a person watching the TV confirmed picture and sound, pause, play, skip forward and back, a quality change and stop. The phone's volume keys do not change the TV volume. Converted films and other TVs are not tested. Oct 22 on tester34 from a Galaxy S25: the cast controls and the on-screen TV volume slider responded on the phone; picture and sound on the TV were not confirmed by the tester, and the phone volume keys were not retested. Owner-reported, not a helper run: on Oct 22 Nick watched House season 4 episode 2 on a 70-inch Samsung smart TV through a Google Chromecast (details still being confirmed; no label or percentage changed).

features.name: Browse, search, collections and Request a title
features.evidence: Oct 5 and Oct 13 on the S24 Ultra: films, shows and music filters, search, 101 collections and the request screen opened. Sending a request was not tried. A fuller media-requests and wishlist feature is only an idea.

features.name: Watchlist, favourites, playlists and Surprise me
features.evidence: Oct 13: playlist made and deleted, watchlist add and remove, and the Surprise me chooser opened. Surprise me was not played through; favourites were not tapped. Oct 22: Surprise me opens its own screen first, then starts a film within about 1.5 seconds.

features.name: Library health
features.evidence: Oct 13: it showed real counts of missing posters, unmatched titles and unreachable files, and says nothing is deleted. Rename or match was not tried.

features.name: Accessibility choices: larger text, high contrast, reduce motion, Simple Mode, Caregiver view, captions
features.evidence: Oct 22 test-build update: RETEST-1 on tester35: S9+ checks at 1.5 text size passed for scrolling player tools, visible Download/Watched controls and an unbroken German Home heading. Pixel music/audiobook checks passed at 1.3 text size. These are bounded observations, not 2.0 text size, TalkBack, high contrast, reduced motion or every landscape screen.

features.name: Phone app languages (English plus five)
features.evidence: Oct 13: six languages switched live on Home and the tabs. Much of the app is still English, and no native speaker has read the wording.

features.name: Demo mode (three sample clips, no account)
features.evidence: Oct 13 on the S9+ (one check): the banner, title page, player and Exit worked. The title page mentions a subtitles button that the demo player does not show.

features.name: Wake my PC
features.evidence: Oct 13: the button and its message worked. A real wake of a sleeping PC has not been tried.

features.name: Family Recipes and shopping list
features.evidence: Oct 13: four starter recipes opened, the people counter and a shopping list worked. Amounts, adding a recipe and sharing were not tried.

features.name: Packing list shared between phones
features.evidence: Oct 13 on two phones (one check): add, tick and remove showed up on the other phone within about 6 seconds. Ticking offline was not tried.

features.name: Camp Jobs and Star Chart
features.evidence: Oct 13 (one check): names, a shared job wheel, ticking jobs for stars and removing names all worked. The Add button hides behind the keyboard until it is closed.

features.name: Family Dashboard
features.evidence: Oct 13 (one check): its cards matched the numbers on the other screens.

features.name: Family achievements (opt-in milestones)
features.evidence: In Android 1.51-tester33 and later, off until the host turns it on. Oct 21 on tester33 (a Pixel 3): the opt-in preview text and the two "cannot be undone" dialogs were correct. No milestone was recorded.

features.name: Pet Photos and Explorer badges
features.evidence: Automatic tests only.

features.name: Phone as a TV remote web page, media keys and per-person look-up sites
features.evidence: Built, automatic tests only, not in a finished state.

features.name: Android app on Google Play
features.evidence: Not submitted to Google Play. The Android app is a sideload test download from this site. The offline demo was tried on one phone on Oct 13.

features.name: Phone Help (show your screen to another phone)
features.evidence: Switched off and paused. Not available.

features.name: Android TV and Google TV layout (inside the Android app)
features.evidence: No test on a real Android TV is recorded. The code and its screen checks exist.

features.name: Watch Next row on Android TV
features.evidence: Automatic tests only; no real TV test.

features.name: Link a TV (sign a TV in with a code approved on your phone)
features.evidence: Built; the server switch is on. Never tried with a real TV app.

features.name: Android TV remote focus and readability polish
features.evidence: Written and reviewed; not yet merged into a download.

features.name: Beebo Auto: sign-in, video list, sound and fast-forward
features.evidence: Beebo Auto 1.20 (build 21) has not been tested in a real car. An earlier build had one first check in one car on Oct 6, 2026 (a 2021 Audi SQ5 with Android Auto): sign-in, the video list, sound through the car speakers and fast-forward worked. Video on the car screen, music, car-screen titles, Maps voice ducking, away from home, passenger games, Car Party and other cars are not tested. Labelled Beta because the only car check used an earlier build.

features.name: Beebo Auto: music, car-screen titles, Maps voice ducking, away from home
features.evidence: Not tested in a car yet.

features.name: Beebo Auto: Family Fun and passenger games
features.evidence: Not tested in a car yet.

features.name: Car Party (host in the car, passengers join on a web page)
features.evidence: Oct 13 on two phones at home: the host started a party with a code and QR, a passenger joined and saw what was playing and who was in the car, then left. In a real parked car a guest could follow along and send reactions, but a passenger could not watch the movie and a blank name blocked a guest. That was not a driving test. In the Oct 21, 2026 release, Car Party controls stay usable while projecting; those fixes still need real phones and a real car.

features.name: Amazon Fire TV tester build
features.evidence: An install-it-yourself tester build. Not tested on a real Fire TV.

features.name: Roku channel
features.evidence: Tried in a simulator only.

features.name: LG smart TV app
features.evidence: Tried in a desktop browser only.

features.name: Samsung smart TV app
features.evidence: No install file yet. Tried in a desktop browser only; the TV's web browser works today.

features.name: Xbox app
features.evidence: No download yet. Never built or run on a console; the Edge browser on the Xbox works today.

features.name: Native iPhone and iPad app
features.evidence: Not published, never run on a real iPhone or iPad, needs Apple's approval.

features.name: Native Apple TV app
features.evidence: Not published and never run on a real Apple TV.

features.name: macOS server app
features.evidence: Test builds are made automatically; no person has run one on a real Mac, and it needs Apple signing.

features.name: Any web browser: library and player, served by your own Beebo computer
features.evidence: Oct 22 test-build update: The browser repair has split delivery: the server portion is reported deployed at 6:49 AM Eastern on October 22, with a further TV-browser server repair at 7:24 AM; the desktop-player portion is in unpublished Windows 0.1.100. The affected PC and combined away-route repair still need retesting. Owner-reported on October 22: on a friend’s Samsung TV built-in browser, playback away from home and Skip intro worked after repeated Reconnect clicks; ordinary poster/sidebar navigation failed without that extra step, and Up next/Next were absent at the credits. The fixed-build retry, exact TV model, browser version and served build are unconfirmed. Earlier Chromecast viewing is a separate observation with sender details unconfirmed. No new tick or broad real-world pass. The reviewed web-player Next/Full screen work is not in public downloads. Pages that suppress referrer information and a modeled cross-tab edge case remain qualified. Android version-picker results do not verify the separate desktop version-heading issue.

features.name: iPhone and iPad: add the web app to the Home Screen
features.evidence: Automatic tests only; not run on a real iPhone or iPad. Offline downloads need the Android app.

features.name: Linux desktop (AppImage and .deb, version 0.1.82)
features.evidence: Starts and answers on its web address in an automatic headless check. Not run on a real Linux desktop by a person; not code-signed; older than the current Windows download, and no automatic updates.

features.name: Docker or NAS headless server
features.evidence: Not offered for download right now. Not tested on any NAS model.

features.name: Host start and stop; a guest joins by QR with no account (same Wi-Fi)
features.evidence: Oct 13 on two phones: host start, join, and Stop with a confirmation worked; the guest address stopped answering after Stop. Oct 22 on tester34: a Galaxy S25 hosted and a Galaxy S9+ joined in Chrome; but after the host stopped, the guest page said nothing about it (a fix is merged in the code, not released or retested).

features.name: Guest names without sign-up, and reconnecting after a Wi-Fi drop
features.evidence: Oct 13: a blank name became Guest 1; with the guest's Wi-Fi off for 15 seconds the same guest came back with no re-join.

features.name: Guests browse the host's library; a guest asks, the host approves
features.evidence: Oct 13: a guest saw the host's library, asked to watch one and the host approved it. A film played with sound on the guest phone. Oct 22: with the host's "Show my whole library to guests" switch on, an anonymous guest saw the whole library (16 titles). That is by design and the guest is shown a notice; an anonymous guest is not a household profile, so a child profile's limits apply only inside the child's own app.

features.name: Campsite games (the 42 in the list)
features.evidence: Oct 13: all 42 opened from a guest phone and 41 started against a computer opponent (the 42nd asks the host to pick a list). Only three have been finished by two phones (see the next row); Crazy Eights was played by hand. The other games were not played to the end by people.

features.name: Campsite games finished on two phones: Sea Battle, Reversi and Tic-Tac-Toe
features.evidence: Sea Battle was finished by two people on Oct 13 over a direct Wi-Fi link. Reversi was finished between two guest phones on Oct 14. Tic-Tac-Toe was finished between a Galaxy S25 host and a Galaxy S9+ guest on Oct 22 (one tester drove both phones). Each worked on the routes named, and only three of the 42 games have ever been finished this way. A phone hotspot and a guest on mobile data are not tested.

features.name: Solo and pass-and-play games with no Wi-Fi
features.evidence: Oct 1 on a phone in airplane mode and Oct 13 against the computer opponent: the lobby, rules and computer turns worked.

features.name: Guests join over the host phone's own Wi-Fi or a direct Wi-Fi link
features.evidence: Oct 11: a guest joined over a host phone's temporary Wi-Fi and played Tic-Tac-Toe. Oct 13: two people finished Sea Battle over a direct Wi-Fi. A guest on mobile data is not tested.

features.name: Share the app by QR
features.evidence: Oct 13: a real QR scan opened the page, the file matched the installed build byte for byte, and it installed over the existing app. A phone that never had Beebo and an iPhone are not tested.

features.name: Shared downloaded videos play in a guest's browser
features.evidence: Earlier guest playback had a silent-video finding. In development, in the Oct 21, 2026 release: an H.264/AAC guest copy when the original audio will not play in a browser. What is left: hear sound, seek and save on real guest phones after release.

features.name: Watch together without downloading first (stream once)
features.evidence: Oct 4: one film was shared from a host phone to one guest phone. Oct 13: the size prompt appeared on the host. More films and more guests are not tested.

features.name: A guest saves a shared video to their own phone (host approves)
features.evidence: In the Oct 21, 2026 release: host approval no longer cuts a running guest download. Earlier test-build transfers do not prove the saved copy plays. What is left: a real guest download during approval, followed by picture and audible-sound checks.

features.name: Wireless speakers: guests' phones as music speakers
features.evidence: Oct 13: one guest phone appeared as a speaker with positions and a timing nudge, and the page warns that wireless speakers add delay. A real group and the click test heard by a person are not tested.

features.name: Phone speakers for a film (left, right and surround from phones)
features.evidence: Oct 13: two phones played left and right for a film on a PC; the owner said it sounded great but one phone sounded a tiny bit off. Timing stayed within about 10 ms on average in a 75-second recording.

features.name: Synced group music across phones
features.evidence: Automatic tests only.

features.name: Karaoke and recordings
features.evidence: Automatic tests only.

features.name: Shared photo and video presentation
features.evidence: Not tried with a real audience.

features.name: Roadside Quiz, Campfire Songbook, Night Sky Cards and Rainy-Day box
features.evidence: Oct 5 on one Galaxy S24 Ultra (one check): a quiz question was scored, both songbook chants and line-by-line play worked, the moon phase was right for that day, and the filters worked. On Oct 13 the screens only opened.

features.name: Trip clock and quiet hours
features.evidence: Oct 13: the screens opened with trip length, arrive-at and a privacy line. They were not run.

features.name: Treasure and scavenger hunts
features.evidence: Automatic tests only.

features.name: Walkie-talkie on the same Wi-Fi
features.evidence: Oct 1: browser tests on two phones passed for microphone access and a 3-minute stream. Two phones talking to each other is not confirmed.

features.name: Walkie-talkie from anywhere
features.evidence: The server part is on; the Oct 21, 2026 release is the first app release that uses it. Code complete, off and in the Oct 21, 2026 release: every guest needs host approval, Android has a host panel without a microphone, and each guest has message limits. What is left: real host and guest phones on unrelated networks; the new flow has not been tested on real phones. The server switch being on does not mean it works: nobody has talked through it on real phones.

features.name: Movie Night (TV-led party games, phones join)
features.evidence: Oct 22 test-build update: RETEST-1: the Pixel with tester35 showed a friendly cloud-address explanation and Try again rather than the raw error. It directs the user to the computer’s direct address. This does not test host/create/join/play, a real family session or the full feature; Real device and Real-world remain false.

features.name: Campsite guests who are not on the same Wi-Fi (invite link)
features.evidence: The walkie-talkie invitation and host controls are code complete, off and unreleased. This does not make remote Campsite video or games Available. What is left: release and real-device testing of each supported flow.

features.name: Family Timeline (host-led photo and video sharing)
features.evidence: Being built.

features.name: Portrait Party (private, consent-based photo cards)
features.evidence: Being built. It would be private and consent-based, with no public gallery.

features.name: Start a trip, recap and Present slideshow
features.evidence: Oct 13 on the S24 Ultra: Start trip, We're home, the recap card and a full-screen Present slide worked.

features.name: Save the trip as an MP4 video
features.evidence: Failed in the published phone build on Oct 13. The fix worked on a test build the same day (a 5-second and a 13-second video were made) but is not in a download yet, and the finished video was not played back by eye.

features.name: Private trip link served from your own computer (home Wi-Fi)
features.evidence: Oct 13: a link with a photo and a clip opened on a second phone on the home Wi-Fi; views counted, +7 days, Turn off and Delete all worked. The ordinary link did not open from outside the home.

features.name: Trip link that opens away from home (through Beebo's server)
features.evidence: Needs the owner to switch on a setting. Oct 13: one real test on 5G mobile data opened the page and played the clip. A second person's phone and an iPhone are not tested.

features.name: Guest photos and clips added to a trip (you say yes to each)
features.evidence: Not tried.

features.name: Direct connection away from home
features.evidence: Oct 22 test-build update: RETEST-1 wording was PARTIAL: the Pixel in real airplane mode showed No internet connection on this phone; the S25 with app networking blocked showed Couldn’t reach Beebo from here. The S25 airplane setting alone had left Wi-Fi up. This does not establish a new away-route, direct-versus-relay or server-failure pass.

features.name: Automatic router set-up (UPnP)
features.evidence: Automatic tests only; no router test is recorded in the sources for this page.

features.name: Use your own relay
features.evidence: Documented and covered by automatic tests; no real third-party relay test is recorded.

features.name: Beebo Relay (optional fallback when a direct connection fails)
features.evidence: Oct 13: after the account's relay switch was fixed on the server, a film played over the relay from a phone on 5G. Two people on the relay at once are not tested. Terms are not final.

features.name: Relay self-serve switch-on and usage line
features.evidence: No screen yet lets a person turn the relay on for their own account. Being built.

features.name: Connection route card and diagnosis
features.evidence: Oct 13: the card said direct on Wi-Fi, direct over the internet on mobile data, and Beebo Relay when it was used, and updated by itself within about 30 seconds of Wi-Fi returning.

features.name: Your own address (yourname.beebo.tv)

faq.a: Beebo is a free, local-first media server with apps. It runs on your own Windows computer, holds the movies, shows, music, photos, audiobooks, podcasts and radio that you already own, and streams them to your phone, tablet, TV, car or any web browser. Beebo includes no movies or shows; you bring your own files.

The Windows server and the apps are free to use at home. Optional extras such as Beebo Relay (Beta) and BeeboVPN (In development) are listed with their status, and their terms are not final. Prices are listed on one page only, the pricing page, and Relay is not available to buy yet.
No. Beebo's own code is closed source and all rights are reserved. It does use third-party open-source components, and the apps include a notices screen that lists them.

faq.q: Does my video go through Beebo's servers?
faq.a: Whenever possible, video goes straight from your computer to the viewer. Beebo's servers carry only small text such as sign-in and connection set-up. If a direct connection cannot be made, the optional Beebo Relay (Beta) can carry the video; it is end-to-end encrypted and the relay cannot see it.

The server runs on Windows 10 and 11 and is Available. You watch with the Android test app, in any web browser, or by casting to a Chromecast. Linux and Docker or NAS are Beta. Fire TV, Roku, LG, Samsung, Xbox, macOS and the native iPhone, iPad and Apple TV apps are In development and have not been tested on real hardware.
No. The Android app is a test download from this website that you install yourself. The Google Play version is in development and has not been submitted.

Many things. The full list on this page says exactly which features are Available, Beta, In development or Planned, what was tested on real devices and when, and what nobody has tested yet. Examples: TV apps on real TVs, a real tuner, a real Mac, a real Linux desktop, and most of Beebo Auto beyond one real car check.

faq.q: How is the completion percentage worked out?
faq.a: It is a share-of-list count, not a promise and not an audit. For example, the share of listed features whose label is Available. The rules and the data file are on this page, and the numbers are calculated from that file by a script.

faq.q: What does Beebo keep about me?
faq.a: Your files stay on your own computer. Beebo keeps the amount of data used per account and basic connection records, including IP addresses, for 7 days for abuse checks. Nothing is sold.

faq.q: Do you test on real devices?
faq.a: Yes, on our own devices: a Galaxy S24 Ultra, a Galaxy S9+, a Chromecast TV, Windows PCs and one real car on one drive. These are our own checks, not a broad beta. Every line says what was tried and what was not.
